config.title: Container With Most Water

intro.title: Container With Most Water
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that solves the 'Container With Most Water' lesson, a classic algorithm challenge. You will learn to find the maximum area of water that can be contained between vertical lines represented by an array of heights. The core concept is the two-pointer technique, an efficient approach for scanning arrays from both ends. Using JavaScript, you will implement this algorithm with basic loops, conditional logic, and mathematical calculations. By the end, you will understand how to optimize solutions by reducing time complexity from a brute-force method to a linear scan.
intro.usecase: The Container With Most Water algorithm solves optimization lessons where you need to find maximum capacity between boundaries, similar to how UI layout engines calculate optimal spacing between elements. In responsive web design, this pattern helps determine the best dimensions for content containers, image galleries, or dashboard panels to maximize visible area while maintaining proportions. Frontend developers use variations of this approach when implementing dynamic resizing features in data visualization tools, video players, or collaborative whiteboard applications where available space must be utilized efficiently.

objectives: Implement the two-pointer technique to traverse the height array
Construct a loop that calculates the area between two vertical lines
Manipulate pointer positions based on height comparisons
Initialize and update a variable to track the maximum water container area
Apply the area calculation formula using minimum height and width
Control loop termination when pointers converge
Integrate all components into a complete solution function

content.body: Imagine you're given a series of vertical lines with different heights. Your task is to find the two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container that can hold the most water. This is a classic two-pointer lesson where we'll use two positions moving through the data to find the optimal solution efficiently.
content.title: Introduction

content.body:
1. Apply the two-pointer technique to find maximum area between vertical lines
2. Implement the Container With Most Water algorithm in JavaScript
3. Explain when to move the left versus right pointer to maximize area
4. Avoid missing potential maximum containers by moving pointers intelligently
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: Look at these vertical lines: heights = [1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7]. Imagine two fingers on the array - one at the leftmost line (height 1) and one at the rightmost line (height 7). The width between them is 8 (distance between indices 0 and 8). The container height is limited by the shorter line (1), so area = width × min(height) = 8 × 1 = 8. Can you find a better pair?
content.title: Try it yourself

content.body: Try moving your fingers to different positions. What if you use the line at index 1 (height 8) and index 8 (height 7)? Width = 7, height = min(8, 7) = 7, area = 49. That's much better! But is this the maximum? Keep exploring different pairs - notice how the area depends on both the distance between lines and the height of the shorter line.
content.title: Explore possibilities

content.body: You just explored different pairs of lines to find the maximum area. For a small array, you could check every possible pair, but that would be O(n²) time complexity. As the array grows, checking all pairs becomes inefficient.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When there are thousands of vertical lines, checking every possible pair (n choose 2 combinations) is too slow. We need a smarter approach that avoids nested scans. The key insight is that we don't need to check every pair - we can use two pointers moving toward each other to find the maximum area efficiently.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Show how two indices or pointers can move toward each other to avoid nested scans. We start with two fingers on the array - one at the beginning and one at the end. At each step, we calculate the area and then move the pointer pointing to the shorter line inward. This works because moving the shorter line might give us a taller line and potentially more area, while moving the taller line would only decrease width without increasing height.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Two fingers on the array; move them according to the comparison of heights.

content.body: We'll use two pointers starting at opposite ends of the array. Calculate the area between them, then move the pointer with the smaller height inward. Why? Because the area is limited by the shorter line, so moving the shorter line might reveal a taller line that could give us more area. We keep track of the maximum area found and continue until the pointers meet.
content.title: The approach

content.body:
1. Initialize left pointer at index 0, right pointer at last index
2. Initialize maxArea to 0
3. While left < right:
   a. Calculate width = right - left
   b. Calculate height = min(heights[left], heights[right])
   c. Calculate area = width × height
   d. Update maxArea if current area is larger
   e. Move the pointer with smaller height inward
4. Return maxArea
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Initialize pointers and max area
steps.instruction: Start by creating the function skeleton and initializing the two pointers and maxArea variable.
steps.hint: Remember: left starts at 0, right starts at the last index (height.length - 1), and maxArea starts at 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function should initialize left, right, and maxArea variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to initialize all three variables: left, right, and maxArea.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. We need left = 0, right = height.length - 1, and maxArea = 0.

steps.title: Create the while loop
steps.instruction: Add a while loop that continues as long as the left pointer is less than the right pointer.
steps.hint: The loop should run while left < right. This ensures the pointers haven't crossed each other.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function should include a while loop with condition left < right.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! The loop will continue until the pointers meet.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there. The condition should be left < right to continue while they haven't met.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember: we want to continue as long as left is less than right.

steps.title: Calculate current area
steps.instruction: Inside the loop, calculate the width, height, and area for the current pointer positions.
steps.hint: Width = right - left, height = min(height[left], height[right]), area = width × height.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function should calculate width, currentHeight, and currentArea inside the loop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start. Make sure to calculate width, height (using Math.min), and area.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's break it down: width = right - left, height = Math.min(height[left], height[right]), area = width × height.

steps.title: Update max area
steps.instruction: Update maxArea if the current area is larger than the previously recorded maximum.
steps.hint: Use Math.max to compare currentArea with maxArea and update maxArea accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function should update maxArea using Math.max.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Use Math.max to compare currentArea with maxArea.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember: maxArea = Math.max(maxArea, currentArea) will update if currentArea is larger.

steps.title: Move the pointers
steps.instruction: Decide which pointer to move inward. Move the pointer that points to the shorter line.
steps.hint: Compare height[left] and height[right]. If left is shorter, increment left. Otherwise, decrement right.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function should move the pointer with smaller height inward and return maxArea.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost complete. Make sure to move the correct pointer based on height comparison and return maxArea.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember: if height[left] < height[right], move left pointer right (left++), otherwise move right pointer left (right--).

content.body: Congratulations! You've implemented the Container With Most Water algorithm using the two-pointer technique. Remember: we move the pointer with the shorter line because that's the limiting factor for area. This approach runs in O(n) time instead of O(n²) for brute force. The key insight is that by moving the shorter line inward, we might find a taller line that could give us more area, while moving the taller line would only decrease width. This pattern of two positions moving through the data is powerful for many array lessons.
